items.headline: Unsloth v0.1.47-beta auto-fit triples single-GPU usable context
items.diff_narrative: A net-new local-fine-tuning lead with no June 19 counterpart, taking the lead slot that yesterday's Jumper/Shazeer talent-war story held. The Unsloth stack tagged v0.1.47-beta ("GLM 5.2 + Model Hub + 3x longer contexts") on June 18: a new auto-fit context algorithm paired with multi-token prediction that the project reports roughly triples the usable context fitting in fixed memory, lifting a single 32GB f16 GPU from about 23,040 to 64,000 tokens without spilling and directly lowering the hardware bar for long-context fine-tuning. The release adds full GLM-5.2 support across its high/max/disabled thinking modes in Unsloth Studio, a full-page Model Hub redesign (trending feed, search, persisted state, README previews, faster Xet downloads with HTTP fallback), a --secure Cloudflare-only encrypted-studio mode, restored vLLM 0.22+ compatibility, DeepSeek-OCR vision support, better Blackwell handling, and modularized export/chat/training/recipes. As a beta the numbers are the project's own, but the context-fit gain is a concrete training-side state-change rather than a benchmark headline.

items.headline: Liquid AI ships LFM2.5 350M on-device retrieval models
items.diff_narrative: A new on-device-retrieval story absent on June 19, distinct from yesterday's VibeThinker-3B small-reasoning item. Liquid AI published two 350M open-weight models on June 19 under its LFM Open License v1.0: LFM2.5-Embedding-350M, a dense bi-encoder mapping a document to one vector, and LFM2.5-ColBERT-350M, a late-interaction model producing per-token vectors for finer matching. Both derive from a shared backbone by swapping causal for bidirectional attention and cover 11 languages. The ColBERT variant is reported at 0.605 NDCG@10 on NanoBEIR and 0.694 Recall@20 on MKQA-11, claimed to beat larger competitors, with GGUF builds running under llama.cpp at median query latency below 10 ms on a MacBook Pro M4 Max. Retrieval/embedding models are the backbone of practical RAG, and a permissively licensed 350M pair this fast on commodity edge hardware is exactly the on-device component that lets local LLM stacks do grounded search without a server-side embedding call. As with any single-vendor launch the numbers are self-reported and await third-party reproduction.

items.headline: Coding-agent harnesses: Hermes Blank Slate, Codex Record & Replay, Cisco FAPO
items.diff_narrative: A new agent-harness control-and-security cluster with no June 19 counterpart, replacing yesterday's Hyundai-Boston Dynamics physical-AI item in the bullet set. Three state-changes landed June 18-20. Nous Research added a Blank Slate setup mode to its open-source Hermes Agent framework (June 20): an agent boots with only a provider/model plus File-Operations and Terminal toolsets, while web, browser, code execution, vision, memory, delegation, cron, skills, plugins and MCP servers stay off until explicitly enabled, with the choice written durably via platform_toolsets.cli and agent.disabled_toolsets so an update cannot silently re-enable them, a least-privilege posture for autonomous agents. The same day OpenAI shipped Record & Replay for its Codex macOS app (build 26.616): a user walks the agent through a desktop workflow once and it is captured as a reusable skill Codex re-runs unattended (Computer Use required; not yet in the EU/UK/Switzerland). And Cisco open-sourced FAPO (June 20), a Claude-Code-driven prompt optimizer that evaluates whole multi-step pipelines, attributes failures to a specific stage, and escalates from prompt edits to parameter tweaks to structural rewrites, with a reported +14.1-point mean gain over GEPA across 15 of 18 model-benchmark pairs.

items.headline: NVIDIA SpatialClaw training-free code-as-action spatial agent
items.diff_narrative: A new applied-research story with no June 19 counterpart. NVIDIA released SpatialClaw on June 19, a training-free framework that lets vision-language models reason about object localization and 3D relationships without model- or benchmark-specific tuning. Instead of retraining, it wraps a stateful Python kernel pre-loaded with input frames and perception primitives; the agent writes one Python cell per step into that persistent kernel, doing genuine test-time computation, for example switching from a centroid-distance heuristic to a KD-tree nearest-neighbor search mid-task. Reported results put code-as-action ahead of prior tool-use approaches: 59.9% average accuracy across 20 spatial benchmarks, +11.2 points over the SpaceTools baseline, with the largest gains on dynamic tasks (DSI-Bench +17.6, MindCube +15.3) and consistency across six backbones from 26B to 397B parameters. The work is open (GitHub NVlabs/SpatialClaw, project page, paper PDF), making it a reproducible result rather than a vendor benchmark claim, and it strengthens the broader pattern of agents emitting executable code as their action space.

items.headline: Bay Area AI events calendar rolls forward
items.diff_narrative: The forward-looking three-track events bullet carries over from June 19 with the calendar advanced and nothing yet past its end date, so no entries dropped this run. The soonest upcoming anchor is now the Confidential Computing Summit (June 23-24 at the San Francisco Mint, Linux Foundation and OPAQUE, naming AMD, Google, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Meta and Samsung), followed by Snowflake's virtual Dev Day and AI Tinkerers' Offensive Security Demo Night with sponsor XBOW (both June 25), and the AI Engineer World's Fair (June 29-July 2, with the optional June 28 orientation and the Cerebral Valley hackathon June 27-28). Further out: AMD Advancing AI (July 23), Black Hat USA's AI Summit (August 1-6), SecurityWeek's AI Risk Summit (August 11-12), Hot Chips (August 23-25), the AI Infra Summit (September 15-17), GitHub Universe (October 28-29), OWASP Global AppSec USA (November 5-6), and AWS re:Invent (November 30-December 4). Zenity's AI Agent Security Summit series remains on the watch list, and all three sub-tracks (mainstream dev/data, AI-security, AI-chip) stay covered.

items.headline: Prediction set rotates to single-GPU context, on-device retrieval, and toolset gating
items.diff_narrative: All three predictions are net-new and the June 19 set retires. Yesterday's predictions -- a sub-7B open-weight model posting an independently corroborated AIME score in the 80s by Q1 2027, Google or DeepMind rolling out a named senior-researcher retention package by Q4 2026, and the Commerce Department publishing a frontier-model export-control framework by Q1 2027 -- all drop with their source storylines. Today's three track the new leads: the Unsloth stack documenting a single commodity 24-32GB consumer GPU fitting 100,000-plus usable tokens for a fine-tuning run by Q2 2027, off the v0.1.47-beta auto-fit gain; a mainstream local-LLM runtime or desktop RAG tool shipping built-in on-device embedding and retrieval as a default with no server-side embedding call by Q1 2027, off the Liquid AI LFM2.5 pair; and three-plus more coding-agent harnesses shipping default-deny toolset gating as baseline by H1 2027, off Hermes Blank Slate and the surrounding harness-autonomy cluster.
